contract: Socket.IO outgoing stream_reset: when a requested segment is missing and triggers a transcode restart with a nonzero start time, {startTime: <segment start seconds>, streamId} is broadcast to every authorized socket; a restart at start time 0, a near or completed-stream miss, a miss while resetting and a miss after close are silent.
exceptions: force is not applicable: a reset is triggered by a missing segment request; there is no separate force-reset endpoint.

A reset whose start time is 0 emits no event because HlsRouter.js:88 tests the returned start time for truthiness; the retranscode still restarts. The packet asserts the silence and the restarted stream instead of inventing an event.
The distant-segment trigger is asserted on a dedicated server whose ffmpeg stand-in keeps the transcode running; the reset itself is produced by the unmodified server.
The accepted playback lifecycle packet supplies scoped evidence; its documented Go differences are deliberately not asserted here.

invariants.contract: A missing segment before the start offset of a stream started at 44 s answers 404 and broadcasts {startTime: 6, streamId: session id} once to both sockets of the owner, the admin's socket and another user's socket.

A segment more than ten beyond the furthest produced segment of a running transcode answers 404 and broadcasts {startTime: 240, streamId} once to every authorized socket; a second missing segment while the stream is resetting answers 404 without a second event; a missing segment 0 restarts at the beginning and broadcasts nothing.
A missing segment of a completed transcode, of a closed stream, and a repeated missing-segment request answer 404 without stream_reset and leave the existing segments served.
